sentences.span: We recommend hedging large geopolitical risks through long exposure to deferred refined products rather than crude, as the outlook on the supply side for refined oil products is more unambiguously negative
sentences.why: GS's Struyven explicitly separates crude (moderated by Mideast supply/China demand) from refined products (unambiguously negative supply outlook), matching 'the two have come apart'; Bernstein 17219 corroborates refined product prices/crack spreads near records while crude is only 'somewhat elevated'.

sentences.span: Markets seem to react badly when actual events affecting energy prices occur. Markets seem to react positively to any story, rumor, or hope that is positive.
sentences.why: Academy Securities' stated pattern (positive rumors/hope instantly move oil prices down) is what 'a ceasefire rumour instantly reprices barrels' paraphrases.

sentences.span: remove that shock absorber and GIR says fair value is roughly $10-15 higher
sentences.why: The only 'fair value' estimate on crude in the entire day's source set belongs to Goldman Sachs' GIR (Jared Cohen), not JPMorgan. No JPMorgan-authored document exists anywhere in the day's file list (checked every .meta.json source field), so attributing this fair-value framing to JPMorgan misstates who said it.

sentences.span: Headline and core PCE decelerate to 2.0% and 2.3% 4Q/4Q in 2027 as the oil shock fades
sentences.why: Every source discussing the oil shock 'fading' (MS 17195, SocGen 17163) frames it as a future expectation for 2027, not something already fading last week when the Fed/BoJ hiked. The sentence presents a forecast as an already-realized condition at the time of the hikes.

sentences.span: meeting between Presidents Trump and Xi on Thursday which will likely garner a lot of headlines
sentences.why: The Thursday Trump-Xi meeting is real and corroborated (also in 17205), but no source shows BofA short 2-year Treasuries/$SHY, no source attributes the crude read to JPMorgan, and no source contains a '$16' crude premium figure (GS's own numbers are $10-15 and $20/bbl, from different scenarios) — the sentence bundles a real event with fabricated attribution and a fabricated figure.

This is a self-referential claim about the pulse's own prior trade call from 'last Monday' — it is not a claim traceable to any research PDF in the source set, so no source document can support or contradict it.

sentences.span: increasing their 2027 estimates for global Hyperscaler issuance $400bn to $420bn, a reflection of some modest increased in CapEx forecasts. That number would represent a ~60% increase vs 2026 estimates
sentences.why: MS 17193 shows hyperscaler aggregate FCF collapsing (from $170bn to $35bn, forecast to bottom near -$265bn), and GS 17233 / SocGen 17214 show hyperscalers ramping bond issuance to fund AI capex as a result — directly supporting 'free cash flow no longer covers the spending, so the marginal dollar comes from bondholders.'

This transition sentence sets up a counter-argument that, per s9, does not exist in any source document (no BofA FMS data, no Goldman semiconductor margin claim found anywhere), so the premise that 'the same houses' provide a counter is unsupported.

No source document mentions a BofA fund manager survey or a 33% overinvesting-in-AI figure, and none mentions Goldman equity strategists citing 70% semiconductor gross margins against a 15-year 55% average.

sentences.span: Markets are now pricing in a greater than 50% chance of a hike in October
sentences.why: '>50% chance' priced for an October hike is fairly characterized as 'a coin flip.'

sentences.span: it's hard to not look at two-year yields approaching 4.75%
sentences.why: 2-year yield 'approaching 4.75%' matches '4.744%' (matching on value per the grading note on figure spellings); tied to the same October-hike pricing discussed in the source, supporting the conditional logic that a no-hike outcome would pull the 2-year lower.

sentences.span: funds sold Semis, broader AI Tech, Discretionary and Industrials / Energy exposures, while adding to Hyperscalers, Optical Networking, Cybersecurity, Financials and Materials
sentences.why: The semis-to-financials rotation is real but is reported as a single week's prime-brokerage flow data (around the September FOMC), not a trend running 'since the Nasdaq peaked in early June' — no source anywhere mentions a June Nasdaq peak or a multi-month rotation of that duration.

sentences.span: Less than 30% of S&P stocks are now above the 50-day moving average... Despite the index price action remaining resilient
sentences.why: GS Coppersmith's note is exactly this thesis: the index looks fine while breadth has deteriorated sharply underneath, matching 'damage spread across the average stock while a few names carry the index.'

sentences.span: The BoJ delivered a 25bp rate hike, citing rising upside inflation risks. Sato and Asada dissented in favour of no policy change
sentences.why: The 1.25% hike and two named dissenters (Sato, Asada) are confirmed, but no source anywhere states this is the 'highest since 1995,' gives a '7-2' vote tally, or says the dissenters were appointed by PM Takaichi — those specifics are fabricated additions to a real event.

No source contains a Japan (or any) core inflation print of 1.7% against 1.8% expected, and no source attributes a January 2027 next-hike call to UBS and Goldman jointly (UBS's own note, 17161, projects gradual six-monthly hikes toward a 1.5% terminal rate with no January 2027 date given).
